interpreted_intent: Create one difficult, independently authored render test for the randomized concept phantasmagoria projection: a legible succession of projected spectral images, not merely generic mist or ghosts, staged around an adult original character whose hairstyle and blouse styling draw only from the supplied reference.
subject: an unmistakably adult archival filmmaker with an original facial identity, long dark wavy hair, and a dark blouse
setting: an abandoned aquarium ticket hall with corroded turnstiles, fogged glass, damp tile, and an old projection rig
event: the filmmaker records a salt-stained route map while a visibly ordered procession of projected spectral marine forms crosses the hall
visual_priorities: make multiple separate projector beams and a readable progression of distinct spectral marine images the dominant evidence
keep the route-map recording action and the adult subject's long dark wavy hair and dark blouse clearly legible
baseline_prompt_en: A cinematic documentary photograph inside an abandoned aquarium ticket hall: an unmistakably adult archival filmmaker with an original facial identity, long dark wavy hair, and a dark blouse records a salt-stained route map on a tripod-mounted camera. Behind her, a projected sequence of spectral marine apparitions visibly advances from one form to the next across the tiled wall: a compact jellyfish silhouette, then an unfurling translucent bell, then trailing luminous tendrils, then a dispersed shoal-like afterimage. Separate cones of projector light connect an old rotating lantern rig to each crisp apparition, while slight edge overlap makes their ordered succession readable in one still frame. Corroded turnstiles, fogged aquarium glass, damp reflections, and numbered ticket windows anchor the real hall. Frame the filmmaker, camera, route map, projector, beams, and the full four-stage apparition sequence together in a wide three-quarter view. Use cool cyan projection light against muted amber practical lamps, restrained grain, realistic optics, and materially believable wet tile.
